analyst_view.overall: Unbeaten leaders Lazio (29 points, a club record start under Gattuso) host Lecce (14th, 10 points, three defeats in their last four before the break and among the league's lowest scorers). Zaccagni, Nuno Tavares, Sutalo and Marusic are out, as the numbers assume, so Noslin and Pedraza fill the left side and Doekhi or Provstgaard partners Diogo Leite; Frattesi has recovered from his fatigue with Italy and should start, and Gudmundsson and Rovella are fit for the bench. For Lecce, Pierotti and Ilic are out, while Monteiro and Berisha were still on individual work this week and are doubtful; the numbers now treat Monteiro as available, so a late absence would only take a little off Lecce. A fan boycott slightly dulls Lazio's home edge, and referee Matteo Marcenaro's high card rate (4.5 a game) is already in the numbers, so the view stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals, already cut for Zaccagni (-10.5%) and Tavares (-6%) and raised on Lecce's side for Lazio's missing defenders. Frattesi, Lazio's joint top scorer with four, is fit, and Lecce's doubt over Monteiro is small for a side that scores little, so I stay at about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Without Zaccagni and Tavares Lazio lose their most direct left side, while Lecce have won plenty of corners lately (33 in six); the numbers already see the absences and the form, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards and already add Marcenaro's high rate (+19%) while taking some off for Lazio's calm recent run. Lecce need points and will press, which can bring fouls, but there is no rivalry or suspension threat, so I stay at about 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.7 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting. Lazio's front three of Isaksen, Pinamonti and Noslin with Frattesi arriving from midfield is close to their recent attack, so I stay at about 25.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target, with Lecce's sharp recent shooting (34 on target in six) already counted. Frattesi being fit and Monteiro being doubtful pull slightly against each other, so I stay at about 8.7.
